- **What prompted it:** Prompted in part by a February 2026 news report that inaccurately listed Bemidji among planned Minnesota data center sites; city staff and council opted to get ahead of the issue and study appropriate size/location standards before any proposal arrives.
- **Affected projects:** None named; no data center project is currently proposed in Bemidji.
- **Detailed status:** KAXE reports that the Planning Board voted 6–1 on 2026-09-14 for a moratorium on data centers exceeding 10,000 square feet and cryptocurrency mining facilities of any size; smaller data centers remain permitted and staff were to draft standards. - **Outcome:** One-year moratorium adopted 6-1 (Ward 3 council member Mark Dickinson dissenting) prohibiting data centers over 10,000 sq ft and crypto mining facilities of any size, while staff draft permanent zoning standards.

### Eagan

- **Type:** City
- **Recorded status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-02-17

- **Moratorium ID:** `mn-eagan-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Ordinance No. 643, 2nd Series, adding Eagan City Code Section 12.09, "Interim Use: Data Center Regulations Study," under Minn. Stat. Sec. 462.355, subd. 4. Public hearing and adoption both occurred February 17, 2026; published in the legal newspaper February 19, 2026.
- **What prompted it:** City study of whether large data centers need additional local regulation because of land use compatibility, municipal water and wastewater systems, infrastructure, environmental, and public health, safety, and welfare impacts
- **Affected projects:** Applies to data centers or cryptocurrency mining facilities using more than 20 MW or proposed within 500 feet of residentially zoned or guided property; allows improvements to existing or approved data centers only if they do not allow use above 9 MW
- **Detailed status:** Recorded active; present legal force remains unverified. MPR News reported on July 7, 2026 that Eagan Capital filed its moratorium challenge on June 15, seeking $50,000 and disputing the city’s authority over electricity demand. CBS Minnesota reported on November 9 that the city was separately suing the company over chiller permits, zoning and noise allegations; it reported that the mayor announced the legal action on November 2. These are reported claims and actions, not judicial findings. Case identifiers, court orders, subsequent moratorium amendments and actual project applicability remain unverified.
- **Outcome:** A moratorium challenge and a separate city enforcement action have been reported. Court dispositions and any resulting change to the moratorium’s operative force remain unverified.

### Freeborn County

- **Type:** County
- **Recorded status:** 🟢 Extended
- **Date enacted:** August 19, 2025, reported adoption of the temporary interim zoning ordinance covering data centers; a parallel ordinance covered energy storage systems.
- **Normalized date:** `2025-08-19` (exact)
- **Duration:** Originally a one-year interim ordinance (adopted August 2025); extended for a second consecutive one-year term, through August 19, 2027, by a unanimous County Board vote on August 18, 2026.
- **Current end date:** `2027-08-19`
- **Sectors:** data center, battery storage
- **Moratorium ID:** `mn-freeborn-county-2025`
- **Legal basis:** Temporary interim zoning ordinance on data centers, adopted by the Freeborn County Board of Commissioners in August 2025 (alongside a parallel moratorium on energy storage systems, due to overlapping grid-infrastructure concerns); extended for a second year (through Aug. 19, 2027) by unanimous County Board resolution on August 18, 2026, under Minnesota Statutes Chapter 394.
- **What prompted it:** Regional energy grid infrastructure, high-voltage utility demand, and public safety concerns common to both data centers and battery energy storage systems; staff reported needing the full extended year to finish the data center ordinance after spending the prior year on the energy-storage-system framework.
- **Affected projects:** None named; discussion referenced 8-15 existing Minnesota data centers and 15-20 in planning stages statewide, without naming a specific Freeborn County project.
- **Detailed status:** Active (extended) as of 2026-09-23. The County Board voted unanimously on August 18, 2026 to extend the moratorium on data centers (originally adopted August 2025) for a second consecutive year, through August 19, 2027, finding that allowing it to lapse would threaten public safety and orderly development because current regulations are inadequate. Planning and Zoning Administrator Trevor Bordelon said his office would need the full additional year to develop the data-center ordinance, having spent the prior year on a parallel energy-storage-system framework intended to serve as a foundation for high-load utility planning generally.
- **Outcome:** County Board voted unanimously to extend the county's one-year-old data center moratorium for a second year (through Aug. 19, 2027) as staff continue developing land-use controls.

### 2025 1st Special Session HF 16 / Chapter 12

- **Policy ID:** `mn-2025-1st-special-session-hf-16-chapter-12`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Greg Davids; Rep. Jon Huot; Sen. Ann H. Rest; R; DFL; DFL
- **Recorded status:** Approved by Governor 2025-06-14, 2025 1st Special Session Chapter 12
- **Provisions:** Created a statewide data-center regulatory package. Key provisions include water preapplication review for data centers proposing more than 100,000,000 gallons per year of consumptive use, permit conditions for large water appropriation projects, utility tariff provisions for very large customers, an annual qualified large-scale data center fee based on peak MW, and modified sales and use tax exemptions.
